title: Validate an email
instructorPromptText: Write a C function `int validate_email(const char *email)` that checks if a string is a valid email address, returning 1 if valid, and 0 otherwise. A valid email has exactly one '@', at least one character before the '@', a domain with at least one '.' after the '@', and no whitespace.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program count occurrences of the '@' symbol to ensure there is exactly one?
specGateDimensions.rationale: An email address cannot have multiple '@' symbols. Checking this requires walking the string and counting occurrences.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program verify that the '@' is not the first character of the string (i.e. local part length >= 1)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Ensures that names like `@gmail.com` are correctly classified as invalid by checking indices or pointer offsets.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program verify that there is at least one '.' symbol in the domain portion (after the '@' symbol)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Ensures a domain structure exists, forcing the student to scan the suffix portion of the string.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student accepts emails without a dot in the domain name (e.g., `user@domain`).
Student accepts emails starting directly with the `@` symbol.
Student uses pointer navigation (`const char *p = email`) and helper functions like `strchr` instead of manual index loops.
Student does not check for spaces, accepting strings containing whitespace as valid emails.
Student dereferences past the null terminator if they do not check bounds when scanning characters after the '@'.
